title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency: Counting Late-Notice Days from the Rate Notice on File
content:
**Rate notice compliance note — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.** For the late-notice credit on a room-and-board charge, the late-notice days follow the written rate notice the agreement records. The current private pay schedule is effective 1 July 2026 and the rate change notice period is 60 calendar days in every tier.

| What the agreement records | Late-notice days of the charge's span |
|---|---|
| No rate notice delivery date | Every day of the span |
| A delivery date fewer than 60 days before 1 July 2026, or on or after 1 July 2026 | The days of the span before the delivery date plus 60 days |
| A delivery date 60 or more days before 1 July 2026 | The days of the span before 1 July 2026 |

In each row the days are counted from the first day of the span and are never more than the span's days nor fewer than none.

**Both sides of the 60-day line (hypothetical).**
- Notice delivered exactly 60 days before 1 July 2026: third row — the days before 1 July 2026.
- Notice delivered 59 days before: second row — the delivery date plus 60 days falls one day after 1 July 2026, so the span's days before that later day count.

**Hypothetical case.** For the 31-day span of the month that begins on 1 July 2026, a notice delivered 47 days before that date (15 May 2026) puts delivery plus 60 days on 14 July 2026, so 1 to 13 July — 13 days — are late-notice days. Had no notice been recorded, all 31 days would be.
